name: KY-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Guthrie holds a roughly 780-to-1 cash advantage over Wingfield
Incumbent seeking re-election with no outside spending against him
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 97%
model.rationale: The district's twenty-point Republican lean, Guthrie's overwhelming fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing his win near certainty leave the Democratic challenger, who has raised about $7,500, with no visible path; no polls or ratings suggest any competitive threat.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against Guthrie or an unexpected scandal would be the main way this race becomes competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brett Guthrie, the Republican incumbent, seeks another term in a Kentucky district that has leaned about twenty points Republican in recent elections. He enters the general election with roughly $1.7 million on hand after raising nearly $5.9 million, while Democratic nominee Megan Wingfield has reported about $7,500 in total receipts and roughly $1,200 in cash. No outside groups are spending against Guthrie, and an independent candidate is on the ballot with little visible activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Republican chances around 97 percent. With the incumbent renominated, a vast financial advantage, and a district that strongly favors Republicans, the seat is safely Republican. The main variables are turnout and whether any late outside money appears, neither of which currently signals a competitive contest.
